questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank with the synonym of the underlined word.**

The casual nature of the student __destroyed__ his studies and ________ his future.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Ruined**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The synonym of "destroyed" is "ruined".
 
• **Destroyed **means reduced to a state of complete damage or rendered unusable; brought to ruin. (नष्ट किया हुआ)
 
 
• **Example**: *The city was destroyed by the earthquake.*
 
 
 
• **Ruined **means damaged or spoiled to the extent of being no longer usable or functional. (तहस-नहस)
 
 
• **Example**: *The flood ruined all the crops in the field.*
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

**Complete sentence**: *The casual nature of the student destroyed his studies and ruined __his future. *

options.text: Preparing the tea without boiling water

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: "**People are guilty of the very fault they identify in others.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• **Example**: *It's like the pot calling the kettle black when Mark criticized Sarah for being late, considering he's often tardy himself.*
 
 
 
• This idiom is often used to point out hypocrisy or double standards.
 
• The phrase likely originated from the fact that both pots and kettles can become blackened from being heated over a fire.
 
• The idiom can also be used in a humorous or lighthearted way to tease someone who is being hypocritical.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2**.

questions.question:
**Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.**

We __must acknowledge__ the fact that we __had been__ visited Paris many times with friends.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: "**had been**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The sentence is in the present tense, so "**had been**" (past perfect tense) is incorrect.
 
• 
 
The **past perfect tense** is used to indicate that an action was completed or a state of being existed before another action or time in the past.

 
 
• 
 
**Structure**: Subject + had + past participle

 
 
• 
 
**Example**: *She had already finished her homework before the guests arrived.*

 
 
 
 
• The correct verb form to use here would be "**have visited**", which is present perfect tense.
 
• 
 
The **present perfect tense** is used to express actions that happened at an indefinite time in the past, actions that started in the past and continue in the present, or experiences in life up to the present moment.

 
 
• 
 
**Structure**: Subject + have/has + past participle

 
 
• 
 
**Example**:* I have visited Paris several times.*

 
 
 
 
• "**Acknowledge**" and "**must**" are both correctly used in the sentence.
 
• "**Visited**" is also correctly used.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2**.

**Corrected sentence**: *We must acknowledge the fact that we have visited Paris many times with friends.*

Therefore the correct answer is 'Inquisitive'.

• **'Ingenious' **means clever or inventive. It is not a synonym of 'curious'.
 
• **'Indifferent' **means having no particular interest or sympathy. It is not a synonym of 'curious'.
 
• **'Indiscriminate'** means done at random or without careful judgment. It is not a synonym of 'curious'.
